name: Module Lifecycle
description: The single door for installing, activating, deactivating and purging a built-in module for a tenant: the install ledger, the one requires-closure, dependency guards, lifecycle hooks and the data purge. The marketplace storefront, plan changes and tenant provisioning all call it; none of them re-implements it. Whether a tenant may have a module is asked through `module_lifecycle:entitlement`, so this module never imports a billing rail.
author: Kuray Karaaslan

extensionPoints.description: Asked before a module is installed or re-activated for a tenant, and when a billing rail reconciles after an entitlement is taken away: may this tenant have this module? Default export: (tenantId, moduleId) => Promise<{ entitled: boolean, message?: string }>. A contributor returns entitled:true for anything it has no objection to, including every module while its own gate (monetization) is off; a contributor that only caps (source 'ceiling', the platform license edition of fleet_license) is left out when deciding whether the answer is 'plan'; the first objection wins and its message reaches the user as a 403. Declared so module_lifecycle never imports tenant_subscription — the rail needs this module back to close modules on a downgrade, so the arrow can only point inward. With ZERO contributors every module is allowed (standalone installability). FAILS CLOSED: a contributor that throws is 'cannot answer', not 'entitled', and denies with a 503. Contributions are NOT filtered by the tenant's enabled modules — a tenant that switches the billing rail off must not bypass it.

A host that stores keys of other modules' contributions in its own data (an automation flow's node types, a board's widgets, a page's blocks, a setting naming a provider) answers for them here (docs/phases/37-extensions/06). Default export: ReferenceHolder { listReferences(tenantId, moduleId) => { label, count, sample? }, sweep(tenantId, moduleId) => { removed } }. listReferences feeds the impact preview before a deactivation or uninstall and the orphan report; sweep runs only when the module's data is purged, never on disable. A data-gate point: a holder answers whatever its own state.

extensions.description: Modules uninstalled inside their restore window are `uninstalled`, with the date they can be restored until.

Phase 55: the signal kinds this module emits (the audit actions it writes: modules installed, turned on and off, uninstalled, restored and deleted, a tenant's module policy, the platform's module availability and bans), each attribute with its personal-data class. Read by ai_firewall through its registry; imports only the contract from common.
